How it behaves

  • Save needs the six parts agreed and nothing else. The check is an extra step: run it or not, Save is live the moment the sixth part is agreed.
  • Apply to plan needs a saved Foundation. It is dimmed until Save has been pressed once, and it always applies the last saved version, never what is half-typed on the cards.
  • Saving does not freeze the cards. Editing any card after a save starts the next version. v1 stays on the rail untouched until v2 is saved.
  • Save writes a deliverable only. Nothing reaches the plan until Apply is pressed, exactly as today.
  • Applying writes the six parts into the unit's Foundation page (Strategy › Foundation) and replaces the Foundation the plan already holds. The deliverable records that it was applied and when.
  • The same Apply row sits on the deliverable page, so a Foundation saved last week can be applied from the rail without reopening the flow.
  • The chat loses its Save line. The to-do list keeps Consistency check, marked Optional.

Five things to confirm

  1. Replace or not? Mobile's plan already holds a Foundation. Drawn as: applying replaces it, and the page says so before the press. Should it ask for a confirmation first?
  2. Is applying reversible? Drawn as: the old Foundation is kept in the plan's archive, the same way an uploaded plan archives the one it replaces, so it can be put back. Confirm.
  3. After applying, where does the next edit go? Drawn as: editing the cards starts v2 in Deliverables only; the plan keeps what was applied until v2 is applied too. Confirm.
  4. Apply on the deliverable page as well as on the cards? Drawn with both. Keep both, or the cards only?
  5. The deliverable view as six cards. Today it is one run of text. The cards read better and match the flow; confirm, or keep the text.

The pictures come from the platform driven by its own check harness, which is why an amber “viewing as” strip and the harness's own stand-in answers appear in the chat. None of that is part of the proposal.
